title: Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 — Regulation 111: Dimensions of Galleries
text: Regulation 111 dictates the dimensions of workings. In any coal seam, the height of galleries shall not exceed 3.0 metres, and the width of galleries shall not exceed 4.8 metres, except with prior written permission of the Chief Inspector of Mines. Over-width galleries create excessive unsupported roof spans and drastically escalate tensile bending stress.

title: Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 — Regulation 112: Depillaring Operations
text: Regulation 112 specifies extraction of coal pillars (depillaring). Secondary extraction creates front and side abutment stress concentrations. Systematic withdrawal and erection of cogs, breaker props at the goaf edge, and strata monitoring must be strictly executed in compliance with permission conditions approved by the Directorate General of Mines Safety.

title: Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 — Regulation 123: Support of Workings & Systematic Support Rules
text: Regulation 123 mandates that the roof and sides of every working place shall be made secure. The owner, agent, and manager of every mine shall frame Systematic Support Rules (SSR) / Strata Control and Monitoring Plan (SCAMP) specifying the materials, pattern, and intervals of supports. No person shall be deployed under unsupported roof.

title: Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 — Regulation 125: Setting of Supports & Roof Bolting
text: Regulation 125 governs the setting and testing of roof bolts and supports. Every prop, cog, and roof bolt shall be set securely and tested. Mechanized roof bolting with full-column resin or cement capsules must meet anchorage standards. Regular pull tests must verify that anchorage capacity conforms to approved design (>8-10 tonnes).

title: Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 — Regulation 129: Duties of Mining Sirdars & Overmen
text: Regulation 129 stipulates that competent supervisory officials (Overmen and Mining Sirdars) shall carry out thorough inspections of the roof and sides of every working place and roadway before allowing work persons to enter. Sounding tests with a testing rod must be systematically conducted to detect hidden cracks and drummy strata.

title: Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 — Regulation 112: Securing of Workings
text: Regulation 112 of MMR 1961 mandates the securing of stopes, drives, crosscuts, and underground workings in metalliferous mines (copper, zinc, manganese, gold, uranium). Strict dress-down procedures, scaling bars, cable bolting in wide stopes, and ground movement monitoring are legally enforceable requirements.
